title: MnTe direct-3D GW: Gamma ReSigc ~ -1390 eV despite a verified PSD Coulomb - OPEN
symptom: On the direct-reciprocal 3D chain with a fresh, fully PSD Coulomb family (all 65 q positive), the regular-mesh self-energy at Gamma reaches ~ -1390 eV (state 21); path-frontier gaps of ~ -951 eV appear. Solver, auxiliary basis, compression, and frequency-count controls all leave it unchanged; LU makes the program finish but the numbers are garbage (-8400..-24000 eV).
root_cause: Unresolved. Excluded so far: Coulomb definiteness (fresh direct-reciprocal), matrix solver choice (LU vs Cholesky), orbital/auxiliary basis variants, PBE0 references. A stale remote ABACUS missing the atom-mapping/Bloch-phase symmetry fix was also excluded by rebuild (see that entry).
minimal_fix: Treat as the highest-priority open physical bug; reproduce on the current pinned stack with a fresh producer chain, then bisect the Sigc chain (chi0 -> W -> Wc(R,t) -> set_Ws -> cal_Sigmas) with same-dimension, same-U controls; compare against the FHI-aims+LibRPA route for the same system.
validation: A fix must restore |Sigc| to eV-scale physics and recover the EXX gap invariance checks; the Dojo-NC-SR + TZDP 10au GTH route gives a healthy PBE start (gap 0.199/0.669 eV mesh/path, 170 states, no anomalous droop).
avoid: Re-running expensive variants without a new hypothesis; using LU-completed runs as evidence; blaming the Coulomb matrix that already passes its PSD gate.
